geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the current cantilever macro with a split-wing macro to create a real ground-level opening while preserving the dominant mass ancestry.
Open the mass laterally along its long axis so the access edge can read as a threshold.
Create a clear but bounded void that reads as public space rather than a decorative slit.
Retain a grounded connector so the edited form remains continuous and programmatically legible.
Keep the base substantial enough to support neighborhood-living frontage and hierarchy.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the sealed cantilevered finish with a split-wing/public-threshold macro so the dominant mass can open toward the access edge without losing its primary anchor.
Split along the long axis to create a legible lateral opening rather than a generic block.
Introduce a bounded public seam large enough to register as usable ground space.
Keep a continuous base so the composition remains one building with clear hierarchy.
Preserve enough base width to support active frontage and prevent fragmentation.

rationale: The massing is coherent across views and the bent/cantilevered body gives a single readable gesture, but it does not yet satisfy the neighborhood-living brief. The main failure is the lack of a legible public void or active ground threshold at the verified access edge; the form behaves like a compact sealed object rather than a street building. The silhouette is serviceable but generic, with only a mild stepped/tilted condition and no convincing section-program logic for mixed neighborhood living. Repair integrity is strong because the solid remains continuous and not visibly collided. Overall this is an acceptable early massing study, but not program-fit because the ground relation is semantically opposite to the brief.
